children: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate Semicon India 2026 on Thursday, the three-day conference and exhibition, being held between September 17 and 19, on the theme ‘Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem’.
Incidentally, the first day (September 17) coincides with the PM’s birthday.

“The Prime Minister has made electronics manufacturing as a new avenue for employment opportunities in the country. Electronics manufacturing has grown seven times in the last 12 years, exports of electronics by 11 times and generation of 25-lakh people. The way semiconductor or mobile manufacturing are growing in the country, it has made a new identity in the world,” Ashwini Vaishnaw, Minister of Electronics and Information Technology, said.
Semiconductor is a foundational industry and even though attempts were made in the 1960s in India, finally it got successful to establish in the last one decade, he added.

Semicon India 2026 will bring together global and Indian companies, policymakers, investors, researchers, start-ups, academic institutions and students from across the semiconductor and electronics value chain.

Some of the leading companies participating at the event include Lam Research, which has also announced investment of ₹10,000 crore to add its first silicon component manufacturing facility in India, SG Semi, Kaynes Semicon, NXP Semiconductor, Applied Materials, Tata Electronics, NXP Semiconductors, Dixon Technologies, Delta Electronics, Micron Technology, AMD India, IBM India, Fujifilm India, Suchi Semicon, etc.

The event will feature more than 600 participating companies and is expected to attract around 50,000 visitors, with representatives from 52 countries, more than 400 executives and over 150 speakers, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said on Wednesday.

The exhibition will feature six ‘Country Pavilions’ representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State booths, a Startup Pavilion, Innovation Showcase, Student Hackathon and Workforce Development Pavilion, it said.

The conference will also focus on advancing collaboration, investment, innovation and talent development in India. Parallel sessions will cover advancements in the display industry, six Country Roundtables designed to facilitate collaboration and joint ventures, a forum on women’s leadership, among other sessions.

Semicon India 2026 will adopt a comprehensive value-chain approach, showcasing the journey from semiconductor materials, equipment and chip design to fabrication, advanced packaging, electronics and systems. The new ‘Sand to Silicon to Systems’ Value Chain Experience will present this journey across the semiconductor ecosystem, it added.

According to Ashok Chandak, President, India Electronics and Semiconductor Association (IESA), Semicon India coming immediately after the BRICS Summit, provides the platform to translate the strategic vision into industry partnerships and investments.

“BRICS sets the strategic direction; Semicon India showcases India’s ability to deliver. Together, they can reinforce India’s role in building a resilient, diversified and globally connected semiconductor and electronics ecosystem,” Chandak said.

title: PM to inaugurate three-day Semicon India 2026 on Thursday
